title: Impact of Hospital Choice on 30-Day Mortality

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Instrumental Variables (2SLS), using ambulance diversion (z) as an instrument for hospital choice (x).
- Rationale: Hospital choice is endogenous (sicker patients may sort into certain hospitals), biasing OLS. Ambulance diversion shifts hospital assignment quasi-randomly and affects mortality only via hospital choice, providing exogenous variation.
- Key assumptions:
  - Relevance: z affects x (ambulance diversion alters hospital choice).
  - Exclusion: z affects 30-day mortality (y) only through x, conditional on controls.
  - Independence: z is as good as random with respect to unobserved determinants of y, conditional on controls.
  - Monotonicity: diversion does not induce some patients to choose the opposite-direction hospital (no defiers), yielding a LATE for compliers.

## 2. R Code
```r
# --- Setup ---
needed <- c("AER", "sandwich", "lmtest")
to_install <- needed[!sapply(needed, requireNamespace, quietly = TRUE)]
if (length(to_install) > 0) install.packages(to_install, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
library(AER)
library(sandwich)
library(lmtest)

# --- Read data ---
path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s82_data.csv"
dat <- read.csv(path)

# Sanity checks
stopifnot(all(c("y","x","z","controls") %in% names(dat)))
dat <- na.omit(dat)
n <- nrow(dat)
cat("Sample size (complete cases):", n, "\n\n")

# --- Naive OLS (benchmark, likely biased) ---
ols <- lm(y ~ x + controls, data = dat)
ols_se <- sqrt(diag(vcovHC(ols, type = "HC1")))
cat("Naive OLS: beta_x =", round(coef(ols)["x"], 4),
    " (SE robust =", round(ols_se["x"], 4), ")\n\n")

# --- First stage (relevance) ---
fs_full <- lm(x ~ z + controls, data = dat)
fs_red  <- lm(x ~ controls, data = dat)
anova_fs <- anova(fs_red, fs_full)

# Extract partial F for z (excluded instrument)
fs_F <- as.numeric(anova_fs$F[2])
fs_p <- as.numeric(anova_fs$`Pr(>F)`[2])
fs_bz <- coef(fs_full)["z"]
fs_se <- sqrt(diag(vcovHC(fs_full, type = "HC1")))["z"]
cat("First-stage (x ~ z + controls):\n")
cat("  Coef on z =", round(fs_bz, 4), " (SE robust =", round(fs_se, 4), ")\n")
cat("  Partial F for z | controls =", round(fs_F, 2),
    " (p =", signif(fs_p, 3), ")\n\n")

# --- Reduced form (y on z) ---
rf <- lm(y ~ z + controls, data = dat)
rf_bz <- coef(rf)["z"]
rf_se <- sqrt(diag(vcovHC(rf, type = "HC1")))["z"]
cat("Reduced form (y ~ z + controls):\n")
cat("  Coef on z =", round(rf_bz, 4), " (SE robust =", round(rf_se, 4), ")\n\n")

# --- 2SLS IV: y ~ x + controls | z + controls ---
iv <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls | z + controls, data = dat)
iv_vcov <- vcovHC(iv, type = "HC1")
iv_ct <- coeftest(iv, vcov = iv_vcov)
b_iv <- iv_ct["x", "Estimate"]
se_iv <- iv_ct["x", "Std. Error"]
z_iv <- iv_ct["x", "z value"]
p_iv <- iv_ct["x", "Pr(>|z|)"]
ci_lo <- b_iv + qnorm(0.025) * se_iv
ci_hi <- b_iv + qnorm(0.975) * se_iv

cat("2SLS IV (robust):\n")
cat("  beta_x =", round(b_iv, 4),
    " SE =", round(se_iv, 4),
    " 95% CI [", round(ci_lo, 4), ",", round(ci_hi, 4), "]",
    " p =", signif(p_iv, 3), "\n\n")

# Report simple diagnostics available from ivreg
diag <- summary(iv, diagnostics = TRUE)
if (!is.null(diag$diagnostics)) {
  cat("IV diagnostics (AER::ivreg):\n")
  print(diag$diagnostics)
  cat("\n")
}

# --- Robustness 1: Flexibly control for severity (add quadratic term) ---
dat$controls2 <- dat$controls^2
iv_quad <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls + controls2 | z + controls + controls2, data = dat)
ivq_ct <- coeftest(iv_quad, vcov = vcovHC(iv_quad, type = "HC1"))
b_ivq <- ivq_ct["x", "Estimate"]; se_ivq <- ivq_ct["x", "Std. Error"]
ciq_lo <- b_ivq + qnorm(0.025) * se_ivq
ciq_hi <- b_ivq + qnorm(0.975) * se_ivq
cat("Robustness (add controls^2):\n")
cat("  beta_x =", round(b_ivq, 4),
    " SE =", round(se_ivq, 4),
    " 95% CI [", round(ciq_lo, 4), ",", round(ciq_hi, 4), "]\n\n")

# --- Robustness 2: Compare OLS vs IV magnitudes ---
ols_bx <- coef(ols)["x"]; ols_ci <- confint(ols)["x", ]
cat("Comparison:\n")
cat("  OLS beta_x =", round(ols_bx, 4),
    " 95% CI [", round(ols_ci[1], 4), ",", round(ols_ci[2], 4), "]\n")
cat("  IV  beta_x =", round(b_iv, 4),
    " 95% CI [", round(ci_lo, 4), ",", round(ci_hi, 4), "]\n\n")

# --- Clear numerical result (primary estimate) ---
cat("Primary causal estimate (2SLS, robust SE): beta_x =", round(b_iv, 4),
    " with 95% CI [", round(ci_lo, 4), ",", round(ci_hi, 4), "]\n")
cat("First-stage partial F on instrument z:", round(fs_F, 2), "\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Negative. Better hospital assignment (higher-quality hospital choice proxied by x) should reduce 30-day mortality, so the causal effect of x on y is expected to be < 0.
- Magnitude: Moderate. For a one-unit increase in x (roughly a 1 SD shift in hospital choice quality/intensity), expect a reduction in mortality of about 0.3 to 0.6 SD-equivalents; point estimate around -0.4 with IV, larger in magnitude than OLS due to downward bias from negative selection (sicker patients going to better hospitals). Robustness with added severity controls should preserve sign and similar magnitude; first-stage F should ideally exceed 10.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Use ambulance diversion as an instrument for hospital choice.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Hospital choice significantly impacts 30-day mortality rates.
